whatTheRunningBuildProves: A purchased cosmic egg can enter the real Hatching Scene and be reserved once.
The egg can be activated and the hatch can finish in the running browser game.
A procedurally described creature appears and the Confirm contact action becomes available.
The capture uses a company-controlled invented state with no player or child identity.

qualityIssues.observation: The creature occupies too little of the frame to be the emotional focus of a launch image.
qualityIssues.impact: The reveal feels distant and does not communicate the range or detail promised by the wider creature artwork.
qualityIssues.handoff: Give the revealed creature a deliberate close presentation before the decision controls appear.

qualityIssues.observation: The field-classification heading visibly overlaps its own secondary text.
qualityIssues.impact: The first-contact moment looks unfinished and is harder for children and families to read.
qualityIssues.handoff: Reflow the classification card at wide and phone sizes and add a screenshot check for collisions.

qualityIssues.observation: The bottom instruction still says Click egg after the egg has disappeared.
qualityIssues.impact: The interface gives a stale instruction at the most important first decision.
qualityIssues.handoff: Change the instruction state when the creature appears and test the full hatch transition.

qualityIssues.observation: The scan estimate, story prompt, decision control and controls panel compete in the same lower area.
qualityIssues.impact: The reveal has no clear reading order and the central choice loses impact.
qualityIssues.handoff: Simplify the reveal to creature, one short discovery line and one clear action before showing secondary controls.

claimsNotAllowed: This is a polished launch-quality creature reveal.
The screenshot proves a complete hatch-to-first-response sequence.
The creature understands or feels like a person.
The generated marketing artwork is identical to the in-game form.

gameDevelopmentHandoff.requestedOutcome: Make the real creature reveal readable, emotionally strong and visually consistent with the game's honest pixel-and-Phaser form.
acceptanceChecks: The creature is the obvious focus at both 1440 by 810 and 390 by 844.
No heading, label, prompt or button overlaps another element.
No instruction refers to the egg after the creature appears.
The player sees one clear next action.
A fresh automated capture passes before the image is considered for public promotion.

nextCompanyAction: Keep GP-013 as internal evidence. Do not place it in launch posts or press downloads. Recapture after the reveal composition is improved, then review the new frame independently.
